div.div: Every experience climbs the same ladder, and 'done' must name its milestone: simulation done authorises no physical deployment until the cross-target milestone holds

Parameterised over EVERY registered experience, so a new one is covered with no new kernel test. Proves:
- deterministic replay
- safety preemption from every local state
- departure enters common cleanup
- stale session / generation / command / timestamp rejected
- no raw adapter or middleware access
- effect and primitive allowlists; reserved-policy refusal
- materialise before dispatch; cleanup ack before new admission
- back-to-back sessions keep no authority
- bounded timers, queues, retries, diagnostics
- the claim matrix: never two physical actions; audio-out conflict refused; exclusive head refused under gaze; head-defers-to-gaze in BOTH orders
- stuck cancel -> forced cleanup -> recovery
- lease expiry is never quiescence
- readiness fails if the reasoner profile has tools, context, abilities or camera egress (negative test)
- a gesture from a non-participant track is rejected (negative test)

Written per experience (by the authoring agent if agent-authored, and reviewed with the code):
- transition-matrix tests
- policy validation tests
- happy-path and bounded-failure replay scenarios
- capability-degradation scenarios
- expected command and cancellation traces
- projection tests
Scenarios read as given / when / then (BDD): given a state and an input, when the event is admitted, then these effects and this evidence.

Milestone criteria that name NO legacy experience. All three contract kinds added through the catalog and invoked through success, cancellation and failure by a purpose-built contract-smoke experience; one new input added through the catalog; the first-registry experiences (greeting, chat, wave, contract smoke) landed through the authoring flow.
Per experience, on the simulation target; per experience, a clean second browser session back to back with the first.
Hardware-in-the-loop on the robot; sign-off by the architecture and quality reviewers. Agent authorship does not change this gate.

SIMULATION MILESTONE - on the simulation target with no cloud credentials, no network egress, no hardware: rungs 1-4, every safety, authority and cleanup invariant shown by a FAILING negative test, deterministic replay (identical inputs under the replay clock -> identical state encodings, invocation sequences, evidence digests). Showcase artifact: one command -> evidence + a shareable video.
LIVE-CHAT GATE - the real model, on simulation. A cloud outage may block it, never invalidate the offline milestone.

CROSS-TARGET MILESTONE - the same experiences pass hardware-in-the-loop with physical adapter and producer contracts AND give equivalent evidence under the cross-target comparator (C3). Until then every profile is simulation-only and physical execution stays disabled.

A RICH LEGACY EXPERIENCE IS NOT THE DEFINITION OF DONE: an earlier draft made parity with it the exit criterion and bent the platform toward it. It became a required but non-blocking regeneration experiment (C3).

WHAT SIMULATION CANNOT PROVE (C1): contact force or hardware safety from simulated grasp; collision truth from browser monocular depth; perception, conversation, social-timing or manipulation quality; a live human run is never a CI test.

EVIDENCE RULES: every invariant needs a negative test that fails when the rule is broken | schema-versioned evidence carries the full resource lifecycle of every invocation; comparators READ held intervals from these fields and never infer them from presentation events or terminal outcomes | the video illustrates, the evidence proves

Legend: rising steps = the ladder, climbed left to right (each rung's box above it says what it proves) | amber = kernel-level gates | green = per-experience tests | blue = simulation | purple = live model | red = the physical robot and what simulation cannot prove | bars below = milestones and the rungs they span.

Sources. Mechanisms: this kit's notes/ (named per line below) and glossary.md. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown: [Pn] = public (cited); [In] = illustrative (a round design parameter that keeps the design's relations; never a measurement of any system); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/C2-the-conformance-ladder.md (ladder, kernel conformance list, experience suite, milestones, showcase artifact, live-chat gate, cross-target milestone, platform-native done, evidence rules); C1-simulation-first.md (what simulation cannot prove); C3-regeneration-and-comparison.md (non-blocking regeneration, cross-target comparator). Public: Pact documentation, docs.pact.io (consumer-driven contract tests); North, 'Introducing BDD', 2006 (given / when / then). This page carries no numeric design parameter.
